key_facts.fact: Brief v2 cut words per turn from 33.7/32.7 to 20.9/18.7, question endings from 62%/76% to 13%/29%, and stock phrases from 1.8/2.7 to 0.7/0 per call, on the same brains.
key_facts.evidence: 6 simulated callers x 10 turns per brain per brief, convo_bench.py; research/2026-10-20/voicelab/round1-review-and-v2.md

key_facts.fact: Round-1 robotic signature across 316 agent turns: 53% ended on a question, median 22 words (p90 37), 21% restated being an AI, 19% mentioned the link, callback or advisor.

Round-1 human ratings: Gemini 3.1 Live 7.0/10 (2/2 would pick); Sarvam+gpt-oss+Bulbul, Gemini 3.8 Live and gpt-oss+Gemini voice 6.0; Azure-voice stacks 1.5-4.5 with 0 would-pick. Every stack's content was judged robotic.
key_facts.evidence: 65 calls, 33 ratings, 4 testers, n=1-4 per stack; graph measure.2026-10-20.round1-ratings

key_facts.fact: The hang-up guard (goodbye required, caller not mid-question, 1.5 s beat, stays on if the caller speaks) took abrupt agent hang-ups from 17-40% to 0.
The India-hosted all-Azure cascade A has a server reply gap of p50 1,004 ms and p90 1,100 ms. The speculative variant E has p50 823 ms.
key_facts.evidence: 60 turns per config, India VM, no phone leg; research/2026-10-17/lanes/l8-azure-bench/round2/findings.md

key_facts.fact: Lowering latency raises cut-ins. On mid-turn 0.9-1.3 s pauses, cascade A cut in on 72% of turns, B (800 ms segmentation) on 17% and E (speculative) on 100%. Every config took the elderly 2.4 s pause (12/12). There were 0/30 cut-ins on turns without a pause of 0.5 s or more.
Across all of VP's stacks, turn-taking is the binding problem: 15-42% cut-ins, and 100% take the elderly 2.4 s pause.
A quiet elderly 'hmm' (0.45 s) was never transcribed in any cascade or Voice Live arm, so the agent stayed silent. Voice Live returned empty transcripts on 5/14 short answers.
Round-2 smoke reply gaps from India: v2-live 0.79-1.55 s, v2-flashlite 1.6-2.2 s, v2-54mini 2.0-2.6 s, v2-luna 1.9-3.3 s, v2-38flash 2.9-4.2 s.
key_facts.evidence: 1 call x about 3 replies per stack (smoke); round1-review-and-v2.md

key_facts.fact: Voice first audio from India: MAI-Voice-2.1-Flash 425 ms, Gemini 3.8 Flash-Lite TTS 624 ms, Gemini 3.8 Flash TTS 772 ms, Gemini TTS via the Interactions API 4.7-5.1 s. Gemini TTS also adds 0.14-0.36 s of leading silence.

Brain first token from India on brief v2: gpt-oss@groq 535 ms, GPT-4.1 mini 567, Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite 699, GPT-5.4 mini 960, GPT-6 Luna (OpenRouter) 1,438, Gemini 3.8 Flash 1,991, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 2,800. gpt-4.1-mini on a South India Standard deployment measured 304 ms (n=33).
LLM judges ranked Gemini 3.8 Flash best on brief v2 (65/75 win %) and GPT-6 Luna last (28/30). Luna is the owner's pick and has not been confirmed by ear.

Gemini 3.8 Live: p50 1.0 s from India but talks over the caller on 42% of turns. On the paid meter it costs Rs 5.72/min on a 3-minute call and Rs 9-12.7/min on a 10-minute call, because past audio is re-billed every turn.
key_facts.evidence: g5 paid key, n=1-2 calls per cost cell; research/2026-10-18/SYNTHESIS.md

key_facts.fact: Gemini Live's output transcript arrives with or before first audio on 1,041/1,041 turns, so speech-to-speech can be gated by text. The violation-rate battery has not run.
Gemini 3.1 flash live, the round-1 winner, shuts down 2026-11-17 and is not on Vertex.
Gemini API Tier 1 caps 3.8 Flash TTS at 100 requests a day per project per model. Four testers exhausted it within an hour, and 6/12 All-Gemini calls went silent.
key_facts.evidence: 429 error bodies plus lab logs; measure.2026-10-19.gemini-tts-tier1-cap

key_facts.fact: Gemini TTS spoke the 'Say in a <style> tone:' prefix aloud on real Hindi calls. Bracketed stage directions are spoken by TTS in general.
Sound tags (<laugh>, <chuckle>, <sigh>, <breath>) are not spoken by Gemini 3.8 TTS, so they are allowed only on Gemini voices and stripped for every other voice.

Inherited law: sentence-shaped prompt text gets recited (quotes 4/5 to 0 after removal), and position is mechanism (rule mid-brief 0/8, appended last 8/8; brevity 64 to 25 words per turn when placed last).
Metrics do not pick voices: Azure TTS won 15/15 on pronunciation, speed and cost and was rejected by ear as 'not human, not Indian'. An audio-LLM judge rated an American accent 'native Indian'.

Competitor demo agents (US vantage) had clean-turn p50 of Ultravox 1.54 s, Vapi 2.32 s and ElevenLabs 3.75 s, with collisions of 18%, 35% and 3%. Vapi answered a Hinglish caller in Gujarati on 17/18 turns; ElevenLabs answered Hindi callers in English 18/20.
key_facts.evidence: 24 calls, 264 turns, harness bias about 60 ms; research/2026-10-17/lanes/l4b-measured/report.md

key_facts.fact: 0 of 6 competitor dashboards show a predicted reply gap or ship a Hindi or Hinglish backchannel or interruption list. Defaults: Vapi 1.5 s wait, Retell 0 ms added wait, Bolna 500+900 ms, ElevenLabs eagerness Normal.
Bolna's code discards short finals spoken over the agent, drops speech during the welcome, and its use_fillers audio path is dead code.

Large human-vs-AI outcome gaps come from commitment and process, not voice warmth: AI collectors got 21 pp fewer promises and were not hung up on more within 10 s. Up-front disclosure cut conversion about 80% in 2017 but showed no effect in 2026 (n=1,337). Anthropomorphism hurts angry customers.
key_facts.evidence: third-party studies read in research/2026-10-17/lanes/l5-human-dialect/report.md (Choi NBER, Luo 2019, Habel 2026 abstract only, Crolic)

key_facts.fact: No outcome study exists for 'emotional/relational' voice agents in sales. An early-hang-up A/B needs about 686 calls per arm to detect a drop from 15% to 10%.
The Indian phone leg is estimated to add 0.25-0.45 s to the reply gap. No VP call has been timed at a handset.
key_facts.evidence: l8 round2 section 6 (Twilio, Plivo, Exotel docs)

key_facts.fact: Cheapest measured stack C6g (gated Gemini transcribe-live + gpt-oss@Groq + Azure neural) costs Rs 0.94/min AI. The AI budget at Rs 2 ex-GST and 50% margin is Rs 0.54/min. The all-Gemini cascade costs Rs 1.56 (Rs 1.92 from 2027).
key_facts.evidence: usage x list price; research/2026-10-18/SYNTHESIS.md sections 1-2

key_facts.fact: All-Sarvam stack: reply gap 0.97-1.18 s, Sarvam-105B first token about 100 ms, Rs 1.39-1.51/min.
key_facts.evidence: 9 replies, sim_caller.py from India VM; measure.2026-10-19.sarvam-india

key_facts.fact: Rate limits cause silence: a 50k-TPM deployment returned 429 on 13/35 turns at three concurrent speculative streams. One concurrent call needs about 13-25k TPM.
Speculative release on string similarity accepted truncated transcripts 3/58 and negation flips 4/4, so it is unsafe without a negation-aware matcher.

The Taxila Voice Live reference-AEC ear-only front end had 0/66 echo false barge-ins and 12/12 true barge-ins (stop p50 80 ms on the phone-echo harness), but an end-of-turn p50 of 1,480 ms against a 900 ms bar.

Open full-duplex models (Moshi, PersonaPlex, Nemotron VoiceChat) list English only. LiveKit's turn detector claims Hindi TPR 99.4%, but Taxila measured Pipecat Smart Turn v3 at chance (34/72) on child Hinglish.
Round-2 human ratings of brief-v2 stacks have not been collected. The default stack and the brief-v2 confirmation both wait on them, and on the paid Vertex key.

requirements.requirement: One compile() per agent: shapes not lines, script and identity rules at the top, a code-computed agenda ledger plus counts and goal check appended last every turn, and a budget gate that throws on overflow.
requirements.quote: persona_v2.py: 'the counts and the goal check go LAST (a rule mid-brief fired 0/8, appended last 8/8)'

requirements.requirement: A lint in the brief editor that flags recitable sentences and bracketed directions before publish.
requirements.quote: docs/harvest law 2: quotes recited 4/5 to 0 after removal

requirements.requirement: A per-clause code gate before every spoken word. It needs number canonicalisation (lakh, hazaar, Devanagari digits, times), call-level slot memory, a time-aware splitter, and correction of wrong caller figures.
requirements.quote: l8 round2: trivial gate false positives 0-23% of turns; every brain agreed with the caller's wrong premium until a correction rule

requirements.requirement: Disclose being an AI once, lightly, in the opening. The ledger marks it spent; she re-states it only if asked and never denies it. Crisis lines Tele-MANAS 14416 and 112 stay in the brief.
requirements.quote: round 1: 21% of turns restated 'I'm an AI assistant'

requirements.requirement: A pause-aware release policy with continuation-word hold, withdraw-if-caller-resumes, and barge-in on words not coughs. Target ≤5% cut-ins at p50 ≤1.2 s, including the elderly 2.4 s pause.

Ship Hindi and Hinglish backchannel, stop and acknowledgement lists as editable defaults. Short replies (haan, nahi, ruko, bas) are classified, never discarded, and listening stays on during the opening line.
requirements.quote: walkthroughs SYNTHESIS: 0 of 6 ship an editable Hindi or Hinglish backchannel list

requirements.requirement: A silence-timer continuer: a gated 'जी?' after about 2 s of VAD speech with no STT final, so quiet elderly backchannels are not met with silence.
requirements.quote: l8 round2 failure mode 4: 'हम्म…' was missed every time

requirements.requirement: Show a predicted reply gap (endpoint + hold + brain TTFT + voice first audio + phone leg) beside the India-measured p50/p90 for every stack choice. Store the combination that actually ran on each call.
Use India-region deployments, warm TTS pools, a short opening clause and reasoning effort none. Size quota per concurrent call and treat a 429 as a quality incident.
requirements.quote: l8 round2: opening clause 19-29 ms; 429 on 13/35 turns

requirements.requirement: Choose voices only through a blind ear test with accent as its own axis and words per turn as a first-class metric; LLM judges only rank. Run a listener panel with human telecaller references before claiming human-like.
requirements.quote: law 26: Azure TTS won every metric and lost by ear

requirements.requirement: Expressive control per voice: sound tags only where the engine does not speak them (Gemini TTS), tone notes mapped to styles (MAI), everything else stripped. Add a speaking-rate control and a laugh cap enforced by the ledger.
requirements.quote: decision.2026-10-20.sound-tags-gemini-only; round 1 bug: 'speak faster' had no effect

requirements.requirement: The agent ends the call herself with the hang-up guard (goodbye required, not after a caller question, 1.5 s beat, stays on if the caller speaks). Add a silence ladder (nudge in the caller's language, then a polite close) and voicemail detection tuned on Indian operator announcements.
The voice stack is user-selectable with curated defaults. The default is chosen after round-2 human ratings, and a second voice path stays ready in case Google access fails.

Per-contact memory stores preferences only (form of address, language mix, pace, shared context, open promises), never company facts or the agent's own claims. Add an elderly or slow-speech preset and learn pace per contact.
Tune endpointing per segment from measured cut-in rates and early hang-ups. Never use daily K=2 dashboards (52-62% false winners in A/A).

Built-in Hinglish caller simulations (busy, skeptic, worried elder with a 2.4 s pause, angry, confused, noisy street) that report reply gap, cut-ins, language hold, words per turn and question endings, and can gate publish.
Lock the reply language to the caller's mix (Hinglish default), with an explicit language setting and no auto-detect drift.
requirements.quote: l4b: Vapi Gujarati 17/18; S2S drifted to English 5/28 and 7/29

requirements.requirement: Run a non-speech probe (n≥30) before any ASR writes to the CRM, and never put vocabulary lists in free-text ASR prompts.
requirements.quote: law 27; open ASR fabricated on 30/30 non-speech clips
